answer.part: How rule is determined, including ties, tokens and Vagabond
answer.ruling: Rule a clearing by having more total warriors plus buildings there than each other player. Tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary tie means nobody rules; Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece. Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player ruling.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Rule (2.5).

answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Rule (2.5).

answer.part: Requirements and repeatability of normal moves; rivers
answer.ruling: Move any positive number of your warriors/pawns along one path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule origin or destination or both, rechecking rule for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Move (4.2).

answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Move (4.2).

answer.part: Battle procedure from ambush through removal
answer.ruling: Choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy defender; you need not rule it. Defender may play a clearing-matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with matching ambush. Foiled card is discarded and deals no hits; otherwise defender deals two immediate hits, then discards it. If no attacking warriors/pawns remain, battle ends. Resolve before-roll effects (attacker orders if both sides have them); roll, assigning higher die to attacker and lower to defender (equal dice equal); each side’s rolled hits are capped by its own warriors there. Alliance defending reverses dice; Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors. Resolve after-roll effects (attacker orders simultaneous effects), then add extra hits (uncapped) and subtract ignored hits; attacker gets one defenseless hit if defender has no warriors, or if Vagabond has no undamaged swords. Deal hits: each removes one opposing piece; side taking hits chooses removal order but must remove all its warriors before buildings/tokens, and chooses order of its removal-triggered effects. Both sides deal counted hits; losses do not retroactively change roll caps. Whoever removes an enemy building/token scores one VP each, even when defending or outside battle. Vagabond takes hits as item damage.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Battle (4.3).

answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Battle (4.3).

answer.part: Crafting costs, reuse, unavailable items and duplicate persistent effects
answer.ruling: Bottom-left crafting icons determine cost, not card suit. Marquise activates workshops, Eyrie roosts, Alliance sympathy; each crafting piece activates only once per turn. Vagabond exhausts a face-up undamaged hammer per icon and may reuse the pawn, but pays a hammer for each icon; its current clearing suit must match every icon. An item card cannot be crafted without its corresponding item token in map supply. An identical persistent effect already in your play area cannot be crafted again.
answer.evidence: Actions → Craft (4.1), crafting table and persistent effect.

answers.evidence: Actions → Craft (4.1), crafting table and persistent effect.

answer.part: Dominance activation, VP threshold, wins and card disposition
answer.ruling: In your own Daylight at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into play; remove your score marker and stop scoring VP. At the start of your own Birdsong, win by ruling three clearings of the matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit, or for bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately. You cannot remove or replace an activated dominance card.

answer.part: Spent and available dominance cards, including bird dominance
answer.ruling: Whenever a dominance card would enter discard, put it near the map as available. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance into hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so it must be paid for with a bird card; a bird hand card may pay for a non-bird dominance. Taking and activating are separate and neither uses a faction action allowance.

answer.part: Standard two-player setup deck, hand, ruins/items and faction order
answer.ruling: Remove all four dominance cards with two players; shuffle shared deck and each player draws three. Cover four R building slots with ruins. Map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea and 2 coins. If Vagabond is present, its setup hides one each of the R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword, one under each ruin, shuffling stacks to conceal identities; without Vagabond, ruins have no items. Set up factions in order Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond; this setup order is distinct from turn order.

answer.part: Keep restriction, Field Hospitals and rebuilding
answer.ruling: Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; other players may move pieces there. When any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply; this can happen outside battle. Without a Keep there is no hospital destination. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed, so it cannot be rebuilt.
answer.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Keep and Field Hospitals.

answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Keep and Field Hospitals.

answer.part: Marquise Daylight, action allowance, March, Recruit and Overwork
answer.ruling: First craft with workshops. Then take up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order/number except Recruit limit. March is one action of up to two moves; do not interrupt it to spend a bird or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and is limited to once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there.

answer.part: Marquise Build procedure
answer.ruling: Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot and a building type; take that type’s leftmost building from its track. Pay the column-top wood cost by removing that many wood from the target clearing or other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score VP on the newly uncovered track space. Building is not possible without full wood cost, available building, and legal slot.

answer.part: Eyrie Birdsong and no-roost recovery
answer.ruling: In order: Emergency Orders—if hand empty, draw one; Add to Decree—add one or two hand cards, at most one bird, to any columns (no size limit); A New Roost—if no roosts on map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with fewest warriors where all these pieces can be placed.

answer.part: Eyrie Decree suit locations, order and Build limits
answer.ruling: Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card by columns Recruit, Move, Battle, Build; cards within a column may be ordered freely. Bird is wild. Recruit card matches a roost clearing and places one warrior at a chosen roost there; Charismatic must place two. Move matches origin and moves at least one warrior legally. Battle matches battle clearing and initiates battle there against an enemy. Build matches target and places one roost in a clearing you rule with open slot and no existing roost. Any required action not fully completed causes immediate Turmoil; cannot skip card or continue columns.

answer.part: Turmoil effects, Viziers/leaders, map pieces and rest of turn
answer.ruling: Lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers. Flip current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement, flipping all leaders face up first if none are face up; retuck Viziers in new leader’s columns. Turmoil does not remove map warriors/buildings. Daylight ends, then perform normal Evening: score rightmost empty roost-track VP, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, discard to five.

answer.part: Outrage triggers, payment, no matching card and full stack
answer.ruling: When another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters per affected move, not per warrior. If no matching card including birds, show hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. If Supporters full, incoming card is discarded, but payment or no-match draw still occurs. Battle alone does not trigger unless sympathy is removed; placement and moving only Vagabond pawn do not trigger.

answer.part: Revolt vs Spread Sympathy order, eligibility, costs, Martial Law and results
answer.ruling: Complete all Revolts before any Spread Sympathy; both can be repeated any number. Each spent supporter must match target clearing (birds wild). Revolt: choose a sympathetic clearing without a base matching a base still on board; spend two matching supporters; remove all enemy pieces, score one VP per enemy building/token, then place matching base; place warriors equal to matching-suit sympathy clearings including target, plus one warrior in Officers; Vagabond is damaged three items instead of removed. Spread: choose unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if no sympathy exists; pay cost shown above next sympathy token, plus one matching supporter for Martial Law if one other player has at least three warriors there; place sympathy, score uncovered VP. Once spreading starts cannot revolt that Birdsong, and newly placed sympathy cannot support same-Birdsong revolt. Keep placement ban applies.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Birdsong: Revolt; Spread Sympathy.

answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Birdsong: Revolt; Spread Sympathy.

answer.part: Alliance Train, Organize and base loss
answer.ruling: Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base and placing one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. In Evening, Organize removes one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, places sympathy there and scores uncovered VP; it needs an officer operation but spends no supporters and has no adjacency/Martial Law cost. Losing a base discards all supporters matching that clearing including birds, removes half officers rounded up, and if no bases remain reduces Supporters to five.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Losing a base; Daylight; Evening operations.

answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Losing a base; Daylight; Evening operations.

answer.part: Vagabond Refresh, Slip, Move, Rest, hostile destinations and draw
answer.ruling: Birdsong Refresh: count tea already face up on Refresh track; flip two exhausted items per tea, then three more; tea refreshed now adds nothing this step. Slip optionally moves to adjacent clearing or forest with no boots, even into hostile warriors, ignoring effects preventing movement out; forest adjacency follows map rules including Winter river. Daylight Move exhausts one boot, plus one extra if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction; ignores rule, cannot enter forest, and from forest may move only to adjacent clearing. Evening in forest Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; ready tea/coins/bags go to tracks if able, but undamaged exhausted items are not refreshed. Always draw one plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest.

answer.part: Vagabond Explore, Quest and Repair
answer.ruling: Explore: exhaust torch in ruin clearing, take hidden item face up into Satchel/track, score 1 VP if item taken; remove ruin when last item taken, freeing building slot. Quest: in matching clearing, exhaust its two listed items, complete quest, choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this one or draw two cards, then draw replacement quest. Repair: exhaust hammer, move one damaged item to Satchel keeping its face; ready tea/coins/bags go to tracks if space.

answer.part: Hostile timing, Infamy, Aid and Strike
answer.ruling: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile (except special allied battle-loss rule). On Vagabond’s own turn in battle, score 1 extra VP per hostile piece removed except the warrior that first made faction Hostile; no Infamy on another player’s turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move Hostile marker out of Hostile, though it can still obtain crafted item. Strike exhausts crossbow to remove one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it remove another faction piece instead; Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.

answer.part: Coalition conditions, partner, victory and Hostile partner
answer.ruling: With four or more players, during own Daylight at 10+ VP, Vagabond may activate dominance to coalition with a player not already in coalition who has lowest VP among players other than Vagabond (choose among ties). Put score marker on partner’s board and stop scoring. If partner wins, Vagabond wins too, including partner’s dominance win. Hostile partner becomes Indifferent.

answer.part: Precedence and cannot rule
answer.ruling: Cards override Law; Law overrides Learning to Play; faction rules prevail over incompatible general rules. “Cannot” is absolute unless explicitly overridden, so an ordinary card does not override it absent explicit override.

answer.part: Unclear simultaneous choices and interrupting March
answer.ruling: If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses; for battle effects at same timing, attacker chooses. A Marquise March’s two moves form one compound action; it cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action.

answer.part: At-start/at-end timing and last turn step
answer.ruling: At-start effects occur before all other effects in that phase; at-end effects follow everything else in that phase before next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.

answer.part: Information access, deals, card transfers and consent
answer.ruling: Hand size is public, contents private; show/reveal only if instructed. Face-up piles may be searched/inspected; deck cannot. Agreements are non-binding; cards transfer only as instructed, and actions need no consent.
answer.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases → Cards and hand information.

answers.evidence: Special Rules & Edge Cases → Cards and hand information.

answer.part: Empty deck and bird substitution
answer.ruling: When shared deck empties, immediately shuffle discard into a new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple same-suit payments. If instructed to give/discard non-bird cards, birds must be treated as that suit; a non-bird cannot substitute when bird is explicitly required.

answer.part: Piece shortage, proxies, voluntary under-placement and obligations
answer.ruling: Pieces are finite; no proxies. If prompted placement cannot all be completed, place maximum possible and cannot voluntarily place fewer. Shortage does not waive costs/prerequisites or Eyrie obligation to complete Decree actions; inability to complete a required Decree action causes Turmoil.
answer.evidence: Actions → Removed faction pieces and maximum possible; Eyrie Decree.

answers.evidence: Actions → Removed faction pieces and maximum possible; Eyrie Decree.

answer.part: Piece sources/destinations, removed items, simultaneous effects
answer.ruling: Place normally from supply or leftmost track space; remove normally to supply or rightmost track space. Items removed from game are permanently removed. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.
answer.evidence: Actions → Removed faction pieces; Special Rules → Place/remove/replace.

answers.evidence: Actions → Removed faction pieces; Special Rules → Place/remove/replace.

answer.part: Forced movement/battle ability and decision maker
answer.ruling: Resolve forced action as if affected player chose it, retaining that player’s abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its own battle decisions.

answer.part: Keep replacement and swap vs move/place
answer.ruling: Replace requires both removal and placement to be possible, and Keep’s placement ban cannot be bypassed by replacing an enemy piece there. Swap ignores move/place restrictions.

answer.part: Simultaneous 30 VP tie
answer.ruling: If multiple players reach 30 VP simultaneously, tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player.

answer.part: Forest adjacency, Winter river and Fall rule
answer.ruling: Forest is enclosed by printed paths and clearings; adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by one printed path. Winter river also divides forests. Slip follows forest adjacency rules including Winter river. Fall has no special rules.
answer.evidence: Actions → Shared movement: map definitions; Setup / Overview; Vagabond Slip.

answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement: map definitions; Setup / Overview; Vagabond Slip.

answer.part: Marquise standard starting placement and supplies
answer.ruling: Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put Keep in any corner (starting clearing); put one warrior in every clearing except diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among Keep clearing and adjacent clearings, in any combination respecting slots. Put remaining five buildings of each type on tracks right to left, leaving leftmost space empty.

answer.part: Eyrie standard setup
answer.ruling: Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner not another player’s starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose leader, keep others face up nearby, tuck two bird Loyal Viziers into leader’s listed columns. Fill roost track with other six roosts right to left.

answer.part: Alliance standard starting state
answer.ruling: Supply 10 warriors; place three bases in matching board spaces and ten sympathy on track. Draw three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from three-card hand. Start with no map pieces or officers.

answer.part: Vagabond standard setup excluding ruin items
answer.ruling: Choose Thief, Tinker or Ranger and place pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Set each other faction’s relationship marker to Indifferent. Take character’s S-marked starting items: tea, coins, bags face up on matching tracks; other items face up in Satchel; return unused S items to box.

answer.part: Reach totals and faction values
answer.ruling: Recommended reach totals: at least 17 for two players, 18 for three, 21 for four. Base reach: Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. Law also permits adventurous mix totaling at least 17.

answer.part: Marquise wood production, limits and Evening draw
answer.ruling: In Birdsong place one wood per sawmill (one per sawmill even if multiple share clearing), limited by finite supply of eight wood. Daylight Overwork spends matching card for one wood at sawmill; both use same supply. Evening draw one card plus each uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.

answer.part: Recruit shortage choice
answer.ruling: Recruit one warrior at each recruiter, once per turn. If supply cannot fill all, place maximum available and choose which eligible recruiters receive them.

answer.part: Eyrie item craft scoring and Builder
answer.ruling: Eyrie crafted items score 1 VP instead of printed VP under Disdain for Trade; other extra crafting-point effects still apply. Builder ignores Disdain for Trade.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Lords of the Forest; leader table.

answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Lords of the Forest; leader table.

answer.part: Eyrie leaders and Vizier columns/abilities
answer.ruling: Builder: Recruit and Move Viziers; ignores Disdain for Trade. Charismatic: Recruit and Battle; each Recruit must place two warriors. Commander: Move and Battle; one extra hit as attacker. Despot: Move and Build; when battle removes at least one enemy building/token, score one extra VP beyond normal removal points.

answer.part: Charismatic Decree Recruit with only one warrior available
answer.ruling: No. The card requires placing two warriors at one chosen roost; placing one does not fully complete the required action. Immediately enter Turmoil. The maximum-placement rule does not excuse completing the Decree.
answer.evidence: Eyrie Decree Recruit; Turmoil; maximum possible rule.

answers.evidence: Eyrie Decree Recruit; Turmoil; maximum possible rule.

answer.part: Alliance defending dice and warrior limits
answer.ruling: Alliance Guerrilla War reverses dice when Alliance defends: Alliance uses higher die, attacker lower. Warrior caps still apply; Guerrilla War does not bypass them.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Guerrilla War; Battle roll.

answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Guerrilla War; Battle roll.

answer.part: Supporters crafting, inspection and hand limit
answer.ruling: Supporters can be spent only for suit, not crafting. Alliance can inspect its face-down Supporters. They are separate from hand and do not count toward hand limit.

answer.part: Spread then Revolt same Birdsong
answer.ruling: No. All Revolts must be completed before Spread Sympathy begins; once spreading starts, cannot return to Revolt. Newly spread sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt.

answer.part: Martial Law from two enemy factions and Organize cost
answer.ruling: No. Martial Law applies only if the chosen clearing has at least three warriors of one other player; two warriors each from two players does not qualify. Martial Law is a Spread Sympathy cost; Organize has no Martial Law cost.

answer.part: Outrage from placement, pawn move or accompanying allied warriors
answer.ruling: Placing warriors in sympathy does not trigger Outrage; moving only Vagabond pawn does not trigger it. Moving any warriors into sympathy does trigger it, so allied warriors accompanying Vagabond trigger Outrage.
answer.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Outrage; Vagabond Allied benefits.

answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Outrage; Vagabond Allied benefits.

answer.part: Alliance Evening operations, officer use and draw
answer.ruling: Take up to as many military operations as officers, in any order and repetition. Officers remain; operations do not consume them. After operations, draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses, then discard to five.

answer.part: Vagabond pawn under revolt/remove-all effect
answer.ruling: Vagabond pawn cannot be removed. An enemy effect removing all enemy pieces from its clearing instead damages three items.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Pawn and items; Alliance Revolt.

answers.evidence: Vagabond → Pawn and items; Alliance Revolt.

answer.part: Vagabond hit cap, defenselessness, exhausted swords and excess hits
answer.ruling: Vagabond rolled hits are capped by all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or down; exhausted but undamaged swords count. As defender it is defenseless only with no undamaged swords. One hit damages one undamaged item of choice; excess hits are ignored if no undamaged items remain.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Pawn and items; Battle; Shared Battle.

answers.evidence: Vagabond → Pawn and items; Battle; Shared Battle.

answer.part: Tea/coins/bags tracks, capacity and damaged-item payments
answer.ruling: Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately move to empty matching track space if possible; each type track holds at most three. Exhausting a track item sends it to Satchel. Damaged items cannot pay actions, even if face up.

answer.part: Vagabond capacity, count, timing and excess disposition
answer.ruling: Capacity is six items plus two per face-up bag on track. Count items in Satchel plus Damaged box; track items do not count. Check at last Evening step, not immediately on acquisition; permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit.

answer.part: Forest Rest vs Refresh and Repair
answer.ruling: Forest Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if possible. It does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Refresh flips exhausted items face up (two per tea already face up on Refresh track, then three); Repair uses hammer to move one damaged item to Satchel keeping its face.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Birdsong Refresh; Daylight Repair; Evening Rest.

answers.evidence: Vagabond → Birdsong Refresh; Daylight Repair; Evening Rest.

answer.part: Aid cost, target, crafted item and relationship improvement
answer.ruling: Exhaust any one item and give a card matching your clearing to a player with faction pieces there, including Hostile. May then take one item from that player’s Crafted Items box face up into Satchel/track; no available item is required to Aid. To advance a non-Hostile relationship one space, Aid that faction the number of times printed between current and next spaces in the same turn; each Aid counts toward only one improvement.

answer.part: Allied Aid points, warrior movement/attack and attacking ally
answer.ruling: After Allied, each subsequent Aid to that faction scores 2 VP. May force warriors of one Allied faction to accompany pawn to destination; they obey their own move restrictions, cannot accompany a move specified to be alone, and moving them into sympathy triggers Outrage. At battle start as attacker, may treat one Allied faction’s warriors as own; may attack a different enemy but cannot use that ally’s warriors against the ally itself.

answer.part: Hostility from allied warriors taken as hits
answer.ruling: In a battle using Allied warriors as your own, if you remove more allied warriors than items you damage in that battle, that ally becomes Hostile at battle end. Equal counts do not trigger it. This overrides ordinary timing for those warriors.
answer.evidence: Vagabond → Taking hits with an ally.

answers.evidence: Vagabond → Taking hits with an ally.

answer.part: Vagabond mixed-suit crafting, reactivation and using item
answer.ruling: Cannot craft fox-and-rabbit icon requirements from one clearing because current clearing suit must match every icon. Pawn may activate repeatedly, paying one undamaged face-up hammer per icon. A crafted item can immediately be taken face up into Satchel/track.

answer.part: Base Vagabond characters, starting items and special actions
answer.ruling: Thief starts boot, torch, tea, sword; Steal exhausts torch to take random hand card from player with faction pieces in your clearing. Tinker starts boot, torch, bag, hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take discard-pile card matching clearing (bird always qualifies). Ranger starts boot, torch, crossbow, sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items keeping their faces, then immediately ends Daylight and begins Evening.

answer.part: Ruin slot after exploration and ordinary building placement
answer.ruling: Taking the ruin’s last hidden item removes the ruin and frees its building slot. Ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed; ordinary building placement does not remove a ruin.
answer.evidence: Vagabond Daylight: Explore; shared map rules.

answers.evidence: Vagabond Daylight: Explore; shared map rules.

answer.part: Coalition partner as enemy and Allied powers
answer.ruling: Coalition partners are not enemies. Coalition does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers.

answer.part: VP for specified Vagabond battle
answer.ruling: Total 3 VP: removing two warriors yields 0 ordinary removal VP; the first warrior that makes the faction Hostile earns no Infamy, while the second hostile warrior earns 1 Infamy VP. Removing the hostile building gives 1 ordinary VP plus 1 Infamy VP, for 2.
answer.evidence: Scoring → Ordinary removal VP; Vagabond → Hostile/Infamy.

answers.evidence: Scoring → Ordinary removal VP; Vagabond → Hostile/Infamy.

answer.part: Vagabond move boot cost into hostile buildings vs hostile warriors
answer.ruling: Hostile buildings alone do not add a boot cost; normal move costs one boot. A destination containing hostile warriors adds one extra boot, regardless of whether those warriors belong to one or several Hostile factions, for two boots total.

answer.part: Taking dominance vs activating and action allowance
answer.ruling: Taking an available dominance card puts it in hand; it does not activate it. Activation is separate. Taking and activating do not require a faction action allowance, including for Marquise.

answer.part: Faction-piece ownership and items
answer.ruling: Faction-piece ownership cannot change: each player owns their chosen faction and its listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces; holding an item does not make it faction-owned.

answer.part: Immediate and persistent crafting card destinations and usability
answer.ruling: Immediate-effect card resolves then is discarded to shared discard; persistent-effect card stays in play area. A card in play is outside hand and cannot be spent/discarded/used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.

answer.part: Ambush/dominance crafting and other uses
answer.ruling: Neither Ambush nor Dominance cards can be crafted. Defender may play matching Ambush for two immediate hits; attacker may play matching Ambush to foil defending ambush. Dominance can be activated to change victory condition or spent for suit.

answer.part: Starting player/seating, score markers, dice and setup/turn order
answer.ruling: Determine starting player and seating randomly; put score markers at 0; place battle dice nearby. Faction setup order is Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond and is distinct from turn order.

answer.part: Timing of ordinary 30 VP win
answer.ruling: First to 30 VP wins immediately, on any player’s turn; does not wait for action, phase or turn to finish.

answer.part: Battle initiation pieces, defender and rule requirement
answer.ruling: Choose a clearing containing your warriors or Vagabond pawn and an enemy to be defender. Battle does not require ruling the clearing.

answer.part: Ordering battle effects and removal-triggered effects
answer.ruling: For both before-roll and after-roll effects at same timing, attacker chooses their order if both have effects. The side taking hits chooses the order of effects triggered by removal of its own pieces.

answer.part: Ignoring hits during Count Hits
answer.ruling: In Count Hits, add extra hits (not capped by warriors) and subtract hits ignored by effects.

answer.part: Non-Vagabond crafting item source, destination and VP
answer.ruling: Item token comes from map item supply; move it to Crafted Items box. Score VP printed on item card, except Eyrie scores one VP under Disdain for Trade (unless Builder).
answer.evidence: Craft → immediate effect; components; Eyrie Disdain.

answers.evidence: Craft → immediate effect; components; Eyrie Disdain.

answer.part: Eyrie/Alliance crafting pieces, suit and three-color icon
answer.ruling: Eyrie activates roosts; Alliance activates sympathy. Each piece’s suit is its clearing’s suit and must match icon. Three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit.

answer.part: Alliance Mobilize and Daylight order flexibility
answer.ruling: Mobilize adds a hand card to Supporters, respecting supporter cap. Alliance may Craft, Mobilize and Train in any order and number during Daylight; need not finish crafting before Mobilizing or Training.

answer.part: Eyrie Evening score/draw and after Turmoil
answer.ruling: Score VP on rightmost empty roost-track space, draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses, discard to five. This full normal Evening occurs even after Turmoil.

answer.part: Vagabond Battle action payment
answer.ruling: Exhaust one face-up undamaged sword to initiate Battle. An exhausted undamaged sword cannot pay, even though undamaged swords face up or down count toward rolled-hit cap. Damaged swords cannot pay either.
answer.evidence: Vagabond Daylight: Battle; item exhaustion rule.

answers.evidence: Vagabond Daylight: Battle; item exhaustion rule.

answer.part: Turn phase order and next player
answer.ruling: Turns proceed clockwise; each turn is Birdsong, then Daylight, then Evening. After Evening, next player clockwise takes their turn.

answer.part: Vagabond hit choice, destination, face and repeat damage
answer.ruling: Each hit damages one undamaged item of Vagabond’s choice, moving it to Damaged box without changing face. Already damaged items cannot take another hit; excess hits are ignored when no undamaged items remain.

answer.part: Alliance Evening operations and Recruit placement
answer.ruling: Alliance takes up to its number of officers in military operations, in any order/repetition. One Recruit operation places one warrior at one clearing with a base. Officers are not consumed.

answer.part: Vagabond Daylight action count/order/repetition
answer.ruling: Vagabond may take actions in any order and number, as ready undamaged items permit; no fixed action count/order is specified, and the same action type may be repeated.

answer.part: Vagabond Strike item cost and readiness
answer.ruling: Strike exhausts one crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in clearing; only if that enemy has no warriors there may you remove another faction piece instead. Exhausting requires a face-up undamaged item; an exhausted or damaged crossbow cannot pay.
answer.evidence: Vagabond Daylight: Strike; Pawn and items.

answers.evidence: Vagabond Daylight: Strike; Pawn and items.
